p: The family's earliest known member is the Saxon count Liudolf (d. 866), who held large estates on the Leine river west of the Harz and in the Eichsfeld of Thuringia. About 852 he and his wife Oda, with Bishop Altfrid of Hildesheim, founded Brunshausen Abbey, which after its move to Gandersheim became the family monastery and burial ground. In 869 his daughter Liutgard married Louis the Younger, son of the Carolingian king Louis the German.

Liudolf's son Otto the Illustrious was, according to the Saxon chronicler Widukind of Corvey, already a candidate for the East Frankish crown in 911, when it passed instead to the Franconian duke Conrad I. Otto died in 912, and his son Henry the Fowler succeeded him as Duke of Saxony.

Elected king in May 919, Henry won the support of the Franconian, Bavarian, Swabian and Lotharingian dukes and in 933 defeated the Hungarians at the Battle of Riade. Otto I put down revolts by his brother Duke Henry I of Bavaria and his son Duke Liudolf of Swabia, reducing the dukes to royal subjects, and made the Church in Germany a base of royal power. He was crowned emperor by Pope John XII, married his heir to Theophanu, niece of the Byzantine emperor John I Tzimiskes, and in 968 established the Archbishopric of Magdeburg.

Otto II was defeated by the Saracens at the Battle of Stilo in 982, faced the Great Slav Rising in 983 and died that year aged 28, leaving a three-year-old son for whom Empress Theophanu acted as regent. Otto III installed his confidants Bruno of Carinthia and Gerbert of Aurillac as popes and in 1000 travelled to the Congress of Gniezno; expelled from Rome in 1001, he died the next year aged 21. Henry II, of the Bavarian line, was crowned king on 7 June 1002 and emperor by Pope Benedict VIII on 14 February 1014, and founded the Bishopric of Bamberg in 1007.

Henry II's marriage to Cunigunde of Luxembourg was childless, and with his death in 1024 the dynasty became extinct. The crown passed to Conrad II of the Salian dynasty, a great-grandson of Liutgarde, daughter of Otto I; the Salians held the imperial throne until 1125. Pope Eugene III canonized Henry II in 1146. Historians disagree about how the Ottonians governed: those following Karl Leyser stress oral and ritual means, while others, such as David Bachrach, argue for the continued use of writing in administration.

notes: The article's list says Henry II was 'emperor from 1002'; its text says crowned emperor on 14 February 1014. I followed the text.
Left out the Burgundian inheritance of 1032 (the article's sentence gives 1006 and 1016 in an order that does not make sense).
